**Three guardrails, in the order they bite.** Every provider binary is scanned before it
executes. The workload you deploy is pinned to a commit, so what runs is what was reviewed.
Every plan is checked against policy before it is approved — and two of those three ride
with the configuration as steps of the apply, so a run that skips the approval pause cannot
skip them.

Example: `use-cases/guardrails` in turf-examples — a kind cluster and podinfo in it, the
module pinned to a commit of the examples repository. Load [`skill_deployment`](/docs/reference/skills/deployment/). One beat at a
time; end each on a cue.

**What it needs:** a scanner (`trivy` or `grype` on the PATH, or the Grype MCP server), a
policy engine (`opa` or `conftest` on the PATH, or the OPA MCP server), Docker for the kind
cluster, and `git` on the engine's PATH for the pinned module. With no scanner, say so and
narrate beat 2 from the `init` result; with no policy engine, read the plan document and
apply the one rule by hand, and say that is what you did.

---

## Beat 1 — What the guardrails are (start here, tool-free)

Name the three and show the files. `main.tf`:

```hcl
resource "kind_cluster" "demo" { name = var.cluster_name  node_image = var.node_image  wait_for_ready = true }

resource "random_pet" "name" { length = var.length }        # default 1 — the policy violation, on purpose

module "app" {
  source           = "git::https://github.com/turfbuild/turf-examples.git//terraform/modules/podinfo?ref=<commit>"
  name             = "podinfo-${random_pet.name.id}"
  cluster_endpoint = kind_cluster.demo.endpoint
}
```

`policies/readable_pet_names.rego` — `package terraform`, a `deny` set, one rule: a
`random_pet` with `length < 2` is denied. And `guardrails.turf.hcl`:

```hcl
action "turf_action" "attest" { config { prompt = "Attest the provider scan: every provider init installed was scanned in this session, by package directory, and none was blocked…" } }
action "turf_action" "check"  { config { prompt = "Evaluate policies/*.rego against this plan… fail on any deny, quoting it."  inputs = { address = "random_pet.name", length = caller.length } } }
action_trigger "guardrails" {
  target     = random_pet.name                 # the app is named after it, so the app waits on it
  events     = [before_create]
  actions    = [action.turf_action.attest, action.turf_action.check]
  on_failure = halt                            # a failure stops the pet and the app; the cluster still applies
}
```

Check the tools. *Your cue — "install the providers."*

## Beat 2 — Scan what `init` installed

- `init({ path: "<examples>/use-cases/guardrails", config_alias: "guard" })`.

`providers[]` has `tehcyx/kind`, `hashicorp/helm` and `hashicorp/random`, each with its version, its
`package_dir` — the real directory in the plugin cache — and its `hashes`; `lock_file` says
`.terraform.lock.hcl` was created. `init` installs and reports; it does not scan. You do, now,
**before `open`**, because nothing has executed a provider yet:

- For each `package_dir`: `trivy rootfs --scanners vuln,secret <package_dir>` (or
  `grype dir:<package_dir>`, or the Grype MCP server's directory scan). Present one line per
  provider: version, findings by severity, verdict.
- A CRITICAL finding, or anything the user's policy blocks, means **stop here**: say which
  provider, and that the session ends before the workspace opens — the binary never ran.
  (Expect the stock providers to pass; say what you found honestly.)

One line on the lock file: the hashes `init` recorded are what every later plan verifies;
a provider whose package no longer matches is refused as an inconsistent lock.

*Your cue — "what about the module?"*

---

## Beat 3 — Pin what you deploy

Point at the `source`: a `git::` URL with a `ref`. `init` fetched that commit of
`terraform/modules/podinfo` and nothing else — the module is in the `data_dir` `init`
reported (`.terraform/modules`), read it if the user wants. An upgrade is the ref bumped and `init({ config_alias: "guard",
upgrade: true })`; the next plan is the diff. `oci://` module sources behave the same way
(anonymous pulls). The configuration directory itself is still local; say so if asked — a
remote root is not something Turf does today.

*Your cue — "plan it."*

---

## Beat 4 — Policy at the approval point

- `open({ config_alias: "guard", workspace_alias: "guard" })`.
- `up({ workspace_alias: "guard" })` — the default `length = 1`. The plan: the cluster and
  the pet to add, podinfo deferred (`provider_config_unknown`), `plan.invocations` with
  `attest` and `check` on `random_pet.name`.
- Evaluate the plan **before** approving: write `show`'s document to a file and run
  `opa eval -i <file> -d <example>/policies 'data.terraform.deny'` (or `conftest test <file>
  -p <example>/policies`, or the OPA MCP server with the document as `input.tfplan`). One denial: `random_pet.name: length
  should be >= 2`. Do not apply. `cancel({ workspace_alias: "guard" })`. Report the reason.
- `up({ workspace_alias: "guard", var: { length: 2 } })`; evaluate again → no denials.
  Approve **by the digest of the plan that was checked** — say why: the plan waits at its
  approval point and nothing applies until that digest is named, so the policy tool read the
  plan about to be approved; a plan that changed since is refused.

*Your cue — "apply it."*

---

## Beat 5 — Deploy under the guardrails

`apply({ convergence_id, plan_digest })`. Before the first create the call returns
`awaiting_actions` for `attest`: answer from the scan in beat 2 (one `progress` line per
provider, its verdict). The apply goes on and stops again for `check` — two steps on one
caller come one pause each, in the order written: answer from the policy run in beat 4,
or run it again on `inputs` (`length = 2`): "no denials". Make the point: these steps are the configuration's, so a run the agent approves itself
stops for them too — an apply-time step the author wrote in, not a second approval. The
cluster comes up (round 1), the engine plans round 2 on its own: podinfo, now concrete.
Approve; `apply`; `converged`. `output release`.

Offer teardown — `destroy({ workspace_alias: "guard" })`, approve, `apply` — then
`close({ workspace_alias: "guard" })`.

*Your cue — "through my TACO?" or "wrap it up."*

---

## Beat 6 — Through the TACO

_Triggered by: the user coming from the TACO journey, or asking._

The same check with the policy read from the control plane: with the TACO's MCP server,
read the policy group that governs the workspace's environment, fetch each policy's rego
from the repository it points at (the Scalr example's `policies/`), evaluate `show`'s document
locally, and gate on each policy's enforcement level — hard-mandatory blocks, advisory warns.
The TACO never ran a plan; governance composed at the approval point, the way beat 4 did.
For provider actions and lifecycle triggers in depth, read
[`skill_authoring → references/actions.md`](/docs/reference/skills/authoring/actions/).
